title: Autonomic rollback runner with cost-aware priors and reconciliation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement an autonomic rollback runner that can safely revert configuration changes (batching, caching, routing, quantization profiles) when cost or quality signals breach thresholds. The runner should combine a set of lightweight triggers (telemetry thresholds, error spikes, SLO drift, cost delta), guardrails (rate limits, staged undo windows, state snapshots), and a state reconciliation phase to ensure system consistency after rollback. This ticket covers design, implementation of the controller + reconciler, integration with telemetry/alerts, and a canary rollback workflow for runtime-1.24.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can detect a configured trigger and start an automated rollback dry-run without affecting live traffic
Rollback executor can perform a staged revert (canary -> 25% -> 100%) with configurable safety pauses
State reconciler verifies KV cache and batching shards align with post-rollback config and reports divergence to the console
Cost-aware priors prevent rollbacks that increase expected cost by >5% unless explicitly overridden
End-to-end integration test covering trigger -> rollback -> reconciliation passes in CI and included in runtime-1.24 release notes
runbook: Step 0: Triage - confirm trigger source and scope using /dashboards/rollbacks in Console
Step 1: Launch dry-run in staging via rollback-runner --dry-run --reason='<alert-id>'
Step 2: If dry-run passes, approve canary rollback (25% traffic) via Console or CLI
Step 3: Observe canary for 15 minutes (latency/cost/err rate), abort if regression > threshold
Step 4: If canary stable, escalate to 100% with built-in 5-minute pause between steps
Step 5: Run reconciliation job to validate KV shard checksums and batching configuration hash
Step 6: If reconciliation fails, escalate to SRE on-call and open incident; do not auto-rollback further
telemetry_and_alerts: New metrics: rollback.initiated, rollback.stage, rollback.reconcile_status, rollback.expected_cost_delta
Alert: rollback.triggered but reconciliation_failed -> Priority P0 alert to #sre-rollback
Dashboard: per-customer cost delta and per-model latency drift during rollbacks
Sampling: collect 1% of traces during rollback for offline analysis to avoid perf noise
rollout_plan: Phase A (experimentation): internal-only, enable automatic dry-runs for 1% of config changes for two weeks
Phase B (limited): enable canary rollbacks for non-critical customers and non-production namespaces
Phase C (beta): enable for all hosted API changes with SLA guardrails and opt-out flag for Dedicated tenants
Phase D (GA): runtime-1.24 default behavior with console toggle for AutoRollback (opt-in for Private deployments)
reconciliation_strategy: Snapshot pre-change state: config hash, KV cache checksums, batching shard map
Post-rollback validation: compare checksums and run prefix/KV continuity tests
De-duplication: reconcile TTLs and remove orphaned cache segments older than 24h
Safe-replay: when divergence detected, re-apply small synthetic traffic to warm caches and validate output parity
Human-in-loop: if auto-fix confidence < 90%, fail to manual triage
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: noisy telemetry causes unnecessary rollbacks -> Mitigation: ensemble triggers + debounce window and cost priors
Risk: rollback increases cost -> Mitigation: cost-aware priors refuse rollback if predicted uplift > configured percent
Risk: partial state after rollback -> Mitigation: reconciliation job with snapshot/restore and abort further rollbacks until resolved
Risk: customer-facing disruption -> Mitigation: staged canaries and per-tenant opt-outs
